answer: A marketplace for reef surveys, marble inspections and meadow forecasts could require a paid domain lease for each earning pass. An approved registrar signs the canonical lease ID and a nonrefundable 10-credit yearly fee receipt. Validators verify DNS control and allow that lease ID only one pass per year; subdomains and new payout keys add no passes. A thousand earning aliases therefore need 1,000 distinct leases and 10,000 credits annually. This assumes honest registrars with no rebates; it prices access rather than proving unique operators.
